subject: DPA: interpretation of incident notification windows & subprocessor coordination
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finsecure.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsecure.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying DPA incident notification windows & subprocessor coordination

Hi Laura / Samir —

Thanks for the continued partnership as we work through the DPA details. Two quick items for alignment before we finalize the Incident Notification section:

1) Notification window interpretation: The DPA language says "without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware." Can you confirm whether FinSecure interprets the 72 hours as calendar hours from initial detection, or as business hours from when the incident is triaged? Our legal has flagged cross-border reporting obligations that could be sensitive to the interpretation.

2) Subprocessor cooperation: We want to be explicit about how Redwood will engage subprocessors (forensic vendors, cloud partners) when evidence collection is required. Proposed items:
   - Redwood to provide initial scope and indicators within 24 hours of detection to the customer liaison (we can do a redacted sample).
   - If FinSecure requests onsite or dedicated forensic access to logs or KV cache extracts, we will coordinate a runbook and an access SLA (typical turnaround: 48–72 hours depending on export complexity).

Attached is our incident runbook (redwood_incident_runbook_v1.pdf) showing roles, evidence types, and handover steps.

Can you confirm FinSecure's expectations so we can add precise wording to the DPA (e.g., calendar vs business hours; evidence access timeframe; whether subpoenas/court orders change timing)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if easier.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Customer Security Engagement
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsecure.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finsecure.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying DPA incident notification windows & subprocessor coordination

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the runbook — helpful. A few quick clarifications from ops perspective:

- 72 hours = calendar hours from the timestamp of first detection by the service owner (not business hours). We escalate for any PII exfil indication immediately to our privacy team, but the formal notification timeline is calendar hours.

- For evidence access: FinSecure expects Redwood to preserve relevant logs and retain a copy for 30 days beyond notification unless otherwise requested. If we request an export for our retained forensics vendor, we typically expect that export delivered within 72 hours; if the export requires cross-region transfer we may need an additional 24–48 hours for compliance checks.

Would be great to see a short checklist mapping detection -> preserve -> export -> access, with owners (Redwood ops, Redwood infra, FinSecure forensic lead).

Samir
Director, Infrastructure Ops
FinSecure Corp

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finsecure.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@finsecure.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying DPA incident notification windows & subprocessor coordination

Samir — thanks, that helps.

I pushed a lightweight checklist into the drive link (see related_links). Key items we plan to propose in the DPA text:
- "Notification window" = calendar hours from detection.
- "Preservation period" = minimum 30 days unless superseded by lawful hold.
- Redwood to respond to formal evidence export requests within 72 hours; additional time allowances for cross-border transfers will be explicitly enumerated (up to +48 hours).
- Forensic vendor access: Redwood will coordinate access and provide redacted extracts if full data export is restricted by regulations.

Monica is copied to confirm operational feasibility from the Dedicated/Private infra side. Monica — can you confirm we can meet the 72-hour export SLA for typical KV cache + system logs on Dedicated capacity, and call out any outliers (very large exports, air-gapped regions)?

If that's confirmed, we'll draft precise DPA language and circulate to Laura for legal review.

Best,
Vanessa

Subject: RE: Clarifying DPA incident notification windows & subprocessor coordination

Vanessa / Monica — adding the operating constraints from infra.

- Standard exports (logs + request traces + KV metadata) for Dedicated pools: target 48–72 hours. We can do 24 hours for small-scope incidents (single node, <10GB).
- Cross-region exports (EU <-> US) will need compliance signoff; operationally add up to 48 hours for transfer and encryption wrapping.
- Subprocessors: attached a current roster (subprocessors_roster_2027-06.csv) and flags for those that hold backups or forensic-accessible snapshots. Note: vendor "ForenSight" is engaged for forensics; contract allows emergency evidence exports but requires an authorizing ticket from Redwood security + a customer request.

If FinSecure requires direct vendor-to-customer handoff, we will need a contract amendment for that workflow (can be scoped as an optional addendum).

Marcus Lin
Head of Infra Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finsecure.com>

Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarifying DPA incident notification windows & subprocessor coordination

Thanks all — this is helpful and close to what we need. A few legal clarifications before we sign off:

1) Notification trigger: we need the DPA to specify triggers (unauthorized access to customer data, confirmed exfiltration, or material service compromise that may expose PII). "Suspicious activity" is fine as an early communication, but the formal notice obligations kick on the triggers above.

2) 72-hour window: FinSecure accepts calendar hours language. Please include a sentence that allows for "reasonable extensions where ongoing forensic investigation or third-party restrictions apply," with a requirement to notify FinSecure of any extension and the expected duration.

3) Subprocessor and evidence access: we require Redwood to provide (a) an itemized list of evidence types retained, (b) confirmation of encryption-at-rest for backups transferred cross-border, and (c) point-of-contact for the forensic vendor. The attached doc (forensic_access_clause_response.docx) is our proposed DPA wording — please review and indicate any operational blockers.

If Redwood can confirm the 48–72h operational SLAs for typical exports and commit to the preservation windows, we can move to finalize the DPA text. We appreciate the transparency on ForenSight — please put the vendor's contract appendix into the shared drive for legal review.

Laura Chen
General Counsel
FinSecure Corp
